turns.prompt:
You are given one attached CSV file:
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

No property values are provided. Using your knowledge of crystal optics,
crystal symmetry and structure-property relationships, predict which
candidates have the LARGEST SHG tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select
the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The SHG tensor vanishes identically in any centrosymmetric crystal, so only non-centrosymmetric candidates can have nonzero \(d_{ij}\). Among the latter, the magnitude of the largest component is governed by Miller’s rule (\(d_{ijk}\propto\chi_i\chi_j\chi_k\)) together with the degree of constructive alignment of the NLO-active anionic groups (tetrahedra or lone-pair pyramids). Consequently the biggest \(|d_{ij}|\) occur in non-centrosymmetric structures that combine a small band gap (heavy, polarizable atoms: As, Te, I) with well-aligned polar units.

Inspection of the given lattices and Wyckoff positions identifies five such materials:

- c030 (CdSiP\(_2\)) is the chalcopyrite analogue of ZnGeP\(_2\)/CdGeAs\(_2\) (space group \(I\overline{4}2d\)). Its tetrahedral network and gap \(\approx2.2\) eV produce a well-documented \(d_{36}\approx84\) pm V\(^{-1}\).
- c055 is the 6H polytype of (Al,Ga)As. The polar wurtzite-derived stacking of III–V tetrahedra inherits a \(d_{33}\) comparable to zinc-blende GaAs (\(\sim60{-}90\) pm V\(^{-1}\)).
- c083 (LiAsS\(_2\)) contains aligned AsS\(_3\) pyramids (stereochemically active lone pair) in a polar monoclinic cell; first-principles values reach \(d_{15}\approx80\) pm V\(^{-1}\).
- c038 (Tl\(_3\)SbS\(_3\)) is the hexagonal analogue of the classic IR crystal Tl\(_3\)AsSe\(_3\) (\(d_{31}\approx40\) pm V\(^{-1}\)), again driven by aligned PnS\(_3\) pyramids.
- c039 (RbGeI\(_3\)) is a lone-pair perovskite in which off-center Ge(II) displacements generate a large polar \(d_{33}\) (iodide polarizability further enhances the response relative to the chloride/bromide analogues present in the pool).

All other candidates are either centrosymmetric, possess larger gaps (hence smaller \(\chi^{(1)}\)), or have poorly aligned NLO groups, and therefore exhibit systematically smaller tensor components.

Final: c030, c055, c083, c038, c039
